title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
This page proves the abstract lemma stated on p.96. Setting: M is a set with a symmetric, antireflexive relation ∥, i.e. an orthogonality space. For a part X, X^⊥ = {m : m ∥ X}. 'Supports' are the biorthogonally closed parts S = S^⊥⊥. They form a complete lattice Σ with Inf = ∩ and Sup = (∪)^⊥⊥, and with the orthocomplement ∁S = S^⊥. Symmetry makes ∁ an order-reversing involution. Antireflexivity gives S ∩ ∁S = ∅, and S ∨ ∁S = M. So Σ is a complete ortholattice. In the application, I = F̃ is an index set of strata and A_i = X_i^0. Given a family (A_i) with (a) A_i ≠ ∅ and (b) A_i ∥ A_j for i ≠ j, set S_J = Sup_{i∈J} supp A_i. The claim is that φ: P(I) → Σ, J ↦ S_J, is a lattice embedding preserving arbitrary Sup and Inf, with S_{A∖B} = S_A ∧ ∁S_B for B ⊂ A.

Proof on this page:
(1) Injectivity, in fact order-reflection: S_A ⊂ S_B ⇒ A ⊂ B. This reduces to Lemma 1: S_{i} ⊂ S_B ⇒ i ∈ B.
(2) Lemma 1 follows from Lemma 2: if B ∩ C = ∅ then S_B ∥ S_C, hence S_B ∩ S_C = ∅. This is immediate from (b), since ∪_{B}A_i ⊂ (∪_{C}A_j)^⊥ and that set is closed. Indeed, if i ∉ B then S_i ∥ S_B ⊃ S_i, so S_i ∥ S_i, so S_i = ∅, so A_i = ∅, contradicting (a).
(3) Commutation with Sup is tautological.
(4) For Inf he passes to complements and reduces to the relative-complement formula S_{A∖B} = S_A ∧ ∁S_B. Writing A = B ⊔ B', this becomes S_{B'} = (S_B ∨ S_{B'}) ∧ ∁S_B. That in turn reduces to Lemma 3: for S, S' ∈ Σ with S ∥ S', S' = (S ∨ S') ∧ S^⊥.
(5) He proves the easy inclusion S' ⊂ (S∨S') ∧ S^⊥, since S ∥ S' ⇔ S' ⊂ S^⊥. He then observes that when S ∨ S' = M the reverse inclusion would say S and S' are orthocomplements of each other. He marks this 'Faux'.

Lemma 3 is exactly the orthomodular law, which fails in general ortholattices. On p.98 he builds a counterexample from a graph containing a path A'–A–B–B' and abandons the general lemma. He conjectures the formula should hold for 'variétés' under a divisibility hypothesis, i.e. where the support lattice is orthomodular or even Boolean, as for regular open sets in nice spaces.

Purpose: in the 1986 'analysis situs' notes, the lemma would show that the supports generated by the open strata X_i^0 of a stratification form a Boolean algebra isomorphic to P(strata).
errors: Lemma 3 (orthomodular law) is false for a general orthogonality space. Grothendieck notices this himself ('Faux', and the counterexample on p.98). Hence the claimed commutation of φ with Inf and the formula S_{A∖B} = S_A ∧ ∁S_B are unproven in the stated generality.
The step 'par passage aux complémentaires' implicitly treats ∁ restricted to S_I as a relative complement. That presupposes orthomodularity, or at least S_I = M plus uniqueness of complements.
The parts that are correct as written: injectivity/order-reflection (Lemmas 1–2) and Sup-preservation. These hold in any orthogonality space under hypotheses (a), (b).

ideas.what: Set with symmetric antireflexive relation; biorthogonally closed sets ('supports') form a complete ortholattice with ∁ = ⊥
ideas.modern_name: Orthogonality space and its ortholattice of closed subspaces (polarity / Galois closure)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birkhoff (polarities, Lattice Theory 1940); MacLaren 1964; Dacey 1968; Foulis–Randall

ideas.what: Pairwise orthogonal nonempty family gives an order-embedding of P(I) preserving Sups
ideas.modern_name: Orthogonal family generating a Boolean sub-structure
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in orthomodular lattice theory (Kalmbach, Orthomodular Lattices 1983)

ideas.what: Lemma 3: S ∥ S' ⇒ S' = (S ∨ S') ∧ S^⊥, recognised as false in general
ideas.usually_credited_to: Husimi 1937; Birkhoff–von Neumann context; Foulis, Kalmbach

missed.claim: In tame-topology/stratification notes, Grothendieck independently arrives at the formalism of orthogonality spaces and the orthomodular law, as the obstruction to the strata supports forming a Boolean algebra. This is a link between stratified analysis situs and quantum-logic lattice theory. He does not name it, and the literature does not seem to record it.
missed.quote: Lemme 3 Soient S, S' ∈ Σ, avec S∥S', alors S' = (S∨S')∩∁S ... Faux
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical. It suggests asking which tameness or 'divisibility' hypotheses on stratified spaces make the support lattice orthomodular or Boolean. The mathematics itself is known.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean but standard piece of orthogonality-space lattice theory, rediscovered without naming it, including spotting the failure of orthomodularity. The connection to stratification theory is a curiosity, not a new result.
transcription_corrections: In Lemma 2, 'A, B' is crossed out; the statement reads 'Si B, C ⊂ I avec B∩C = ∅'.
'commutation de φ avec S_γ' should read 'commutation de φ avec Sup'.
The line 'aux Inf [?], par passage aux complémentaires' is duplicated in the transcription; it appears once on the page.
'Faux' is a marginal note in the left margin beside Lemma 3, not part of the statement.
The last line continues: 'à prouver que S, S' sont complémentaires l'un de l'autre' (S ∨ S' = M written with M).
